```{python}
#| output: asis
import json
from html import escape
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import plotly.offline

from pdi import site

eff, meta = site.load("tech-value", "efficiency")
trend, _ = site.load("tech-value", "efficiency_trend")
missing, miss_meta = site.load("tech-value", "efficiency_missing")
sp_proc, sp_meta = site.load("tech-value", "specpower_processors")
sp_trend, _ = site.load("tech-value", "specpower_trend")
mlp, mlp_meta = site.load("tech-value", "mlperf_power")
summary = meta.get("summary") or {"kinds": {}, "electricity": {"usd_per_kwh": 0.17, "fallback": True},
                                   "tco_defaults": {"hours_per_day": 4, "load_share": 0.3, "years": 3},
                                   "job_samples": 10000}  # fmt: skip
version = meta.get("blender_version") or "?"

COLS = ["kind", "model_key", "name", "vendor", "year", "score", "watts", "power_label",
        "power_kind", "score_per_watt", "energy_kj_per_job", "on_frontier", "price_usd"]  # fmt: skip
models = (
    eff[COLS].astype(object).where(eff[COLS].notna(), None).to_dict("records") if len(eff) else []
)
for m in models:
    m["year"] = int(m["year"])
SP_COLS = ["processor", "cpu_vendor", "n_results", "n_vendors", "ops_per_watt", "idle_share",
           "year", *[f"ppw_{p}" for p in (100, 90, 80, 70, 60, 50, 40, 30, 20, 10)]]  # fmt: skip
data = {
    "models": models,
    "trend": trend.to_dict("records") if len(trend) else [],
    "summary": summary,
    "sp": {
        "processors": sp_proc[SP_COLS].head(60).to_dict("records") if len(sp_proc) else [],
        "trend": sp_trend.to_dict("records") if len(sp_trend) else [],
        "n_results": sp_meta.get("n_results") or 0,
        "doubling_years": sp_meta.get("doubling_years"),
    },
}
data_json = json.dumps(data).replace("</", "<\\/")
js = Path("efficiency.js").read_text()
plotly_src = f"https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-{plotly.offline.get_plotlyjs_version()}.min.js"
rate = summary["electricity"]["usd_per_kwh"]


def mlperf_html(df: pd.DataFrame, meta: dict) -> str:
    if df.empty:
        return f'<div class="vd-state">{escape(meta.get("status") or "Not collected yet.")}</div>'
    n_sys = df.groupby(["model", "scenario"])["system"].transform("nunique")
    groups = df[n_sys >= 2]
    singles = df[n_sys < 2]

    def table(part: pd.DataFrame) -> str:
        rows = []
        for (model, scen), g in part.groupby(["model", "scenario"], sort=False):
            g = g.sort_values("perf_per_watt", ascending=False)
            for i, r in enumerate(g.to_dict("records")):
                lead = (
                    f'<td rowspan="{len(g)}"><b>{escape(model)}</b><br><span class="vx-fine">{escape(scen)}</span></td>'
                    if i == 0 else ""
                )
                rows.append(
                    f"<tr>{lead}<td>{escape(r['submitter'])} {escape(r['system'])}<br>"
                    f'<span class="vx-fine">{r["n_accelerators"]}× {escape(r["accelerator"])}</span></td>'
                    f"<td>v{escape(r['round'])}</td>"
                    f'<td class="num">{r["performance"]:,.0f} {escape(r["performance_units"])}</td>'
                    f'<td class="num">{r["watts"]:,.0f}</td>'
                    f'<td class="num"><b>{r["perf_per_watt"]:,.2f}</b> <span class="vx-fine">{escape(r["perf_per_watt_units"])}</span></td>'
                    f'<td><a href="{escape(r["source_url"])}">{escape(r["result_id"])}</a></td></tr>'
                )
        head = ("<tr><th>Benchmark</th><th>System</th><th>Round</th><th class='num'>Throughput</th>"
                "<th class='num'>Measured W</th><th class='num'>Work per joule</th><th>Result ID</th></tr>")  # fmt: skip
        return f'<div class="ef-table-wrap"><table class="ef-table"><thead>{head}</thead><tbody>{"".join(rows)}</tbody></table></div>'

    out = '<section class="vx-card"><h2>Benchmarks measured on two or more systems</h2>'
    if len(groups):
        g = groups[(groups["model"] == "llama2-70b-99") & (groups["scenario"] == "Offline")]
        if g["system"].nunique() >= 2:
            g = g.sort_values("perf_per_watt")
            lo, hi = g.iloc[0], g.iloc[-1]
            chips = (
                f"at {hi['n_accelerators']} accelerators each"
                if hi["n_accelerators"] == lo["n_accelerators"]
                else f"with {hi['n_accelerators']} and {lo['n_accelerators']} accelerators"
            )
            out += (
                f'<p class="vx-strip">On Llama 2 70B (Offline), the {escape(hi["accelerator"])} system '
                f'(v{escape(hi["round"])}) did {hi["perf_per_watt"] / lo["perf_per_watt"]:.1f}× the tokens '
                f'per joule of the {escape(lo["accelerator"])} system (v{escape(lo["round"])}), {chips}.</p>'
            )
        out += table(groups)
    else:
        out += '<div class="vd-state">No benchmark has measured power from two systems yet.</div>'
    out += "</section>"
    if len(singles):
        out += (
            '<details class="vx-more"><summary>Benchmarks measured on one system only</summary>'
            + table(singles) + "</details>"
        )
    out += (
        '<p class="vx-fine ef-legal">MLPerf® Inference v5.0 and v5.1, Closed division, datacenter. '
        "Retrieved from MLCommons' results repositories; result IDs link to each submission. "
        "Results verified by MLCommons Association. Work per joule is throughput divided by measured "
        "system power, derived by this site; it is not an official MLPerf metric. "
        + escape(meta.get("legend", "")) + "</p>"
    )
    return out


def html(fragment: str) -> None:
    print("\n```{=html}\n" + fragment + "\n```\n")


MLPERF_HTML = mlperf_html(mlp, mlp_meta)
html(f"""<nav class="tv-nav" aria-label="Tech Value pages">
<a href="index.html">Value ranking</a>
<a href="fair-price.html">Fair price</a>
<a href="residuals.html">Over &amp; under performers</a>
<a href="efficiency.html" aria-current="page">Performance per watt</a>
</nav>
<div id="ef-root" class="vx">
<script type="application/json" id="ef-data">{data_json}</script>

<header class="vx-head">
  <div class="vx-head-text">
    <h1 id="ef-title">Graphics card efficiency</h1>
    <p>Blender rendering performance for each rated watt.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="vx-head-side">
    <div class="vx-toggle" role="group" aria-label="Part category">
      <button type="button" data-ef-kind="gpu" aria-pressed="true">GPU</button>
      <button type="button" data-ef-kind="cpu" aria-pressed="false">CPU</button>
    </div>
    <span class="vx-checked">Blender {escape(str(version))} · power rated, not measured</span>
  </div>
</header>

<section class="vx-hero" aria-label="Efficiency summary">
  <div class="vx-best" role="group">
    <span class="vx-best-label">Most points per rated watt</span>
    <span class="vx-best-name" id="ef-best-name"></span>
    <span class="vx-best-meta" id="ef-best-meta"></span>
  </div>
  <div class="vx-tile">
    <span class="vx-tile-label">Efficiency gain</span>
    <span class="vx-tile-value" id="ef-trend"></span>
    <span class="vx-tile-note" id="ef-trend-note"></span>
  </div>
  <div class="vx-tile">
    <span class="vx-tile-label">Coverage</span>
    <span class="vx-tile-value" id="ef-cover"></span>
    <span class="vx-tile-note" id="ef-cover-note"></span>
  </div>
</section>

<p class="ef-rated"><b>Every watt on this page is rated.</b> CPU figures are TDP (Intel: processor base power) and GPU figures are reference board power, both from manufacturers' specifications. Real draw during a render can differ by 30% or more, and Intel desktop chips boost far above their base power, which flatters Intel's 65 W parts. Measured power, from SPECpower for server processors and MLPerf® Inference for AI systems, is in its own panel below and never mixed into these rankings.</p>

<section class="vx-card">
  <div class="vx-card-head">
    <h2>Performance vs rated power</h2>
    <label class="vx-field ef-inline"><span class="visually-hidden">Maker</span><select id="ef-vendor"></select></label>
  </div>
  <div id="ef-scatter" class="vd-chart" role="img" aria-label="Scatter of Blender score against rated power"><div class="vd-state">Loading chart…</div></div>
  <div id="ef-legend" class="vx-legend"></div>
  <p class="vx-muted">Hollow dots are rated power. Points above and to the left of another chip do more work on a smaller label.</p>
</section>

<section class="vx-card">
  <div class="vx-card-head">
    <h2>Efficiency ranking</h2>
    <div class="vx-switches">
      <div class="vx-seg" role="group" aria-label="Metric">
        <button type="button" data-ef-metric="ppw" aria-pressed="true">Points per watt</button><button type="button" data-ef-metric="edp" aria-pressed="false">Energy-delay</button>
      </div>
      <label class="ef-alpha" id="ef-alpha-wrap" hidden>Weight on speed <input id="ef-alpha" type="range" min="1" max="2" step="0.1" value="1"> <span id="ef-alpha-val">1.0</span></label>
      <select id="ef-top" class="vx-mini-select" aria-label="How many to show">
        <option value="15">Top 15</option><option value="30">Top 30</option><option value="all">All</option>
      </select>
    </div>
  </div>
  <p class="vx-muted" id="ef-metric-note"></p>
  <div id="ef-table" class="ef-table-wrap"></div>
  <p class="vx-fine" id="ef-count"></p>
  <p class="vx-fine">Energy-delay multiplies the energy a render takes by its time, so a slow chip on a small label does not win just by drawing less. Weight 1 is EDP; weight 2 is ED²P, for work where waiting costs more than power.</p>
</section>

<section class="vx-card">
  <h2>Cost of ownership</h2>
  <p class="vx-muted">Price plus electricity for the hours under load. Idle hours are not charged, because no idle power figure exists yet.</p>
  <div class="ef-calc">
    <label class="vx-field"><span>Electricity (USD per kWh)</span><input id="ef-rate" type="number" min="0" step="0.01" inputmode="decimal"></label>
    <label class="vx-field"><span>Hours used per day</span><input id="ef-hours" type="number" min="0" max="24" step="0.5" inputmode="decimal"></label>
    <label class="vx-field"><span>Share under full load (%)</span><input id="ef-share" type="number" min="0" max="100" step="5" inputmode="numeric"></label>
    <label class="vx-field"><span>Years</span><input id="ef-years" type="number" min="1" max="10" step="1" inputmode="numeric"></label>
  </div>
  <p class="vx-fine" id="ef-rate-note"></p>
  <div id="ef-tco" class="vd-chart" role="img" aria-label="Cheapest total cost of ownership, price plus electricity"><div class="vd-state">Loading chart…</div></div>
  <div class="vx-legend vx-legend-left"><span><span class="ef-swatch" style="background:var(--vd-s1)"></span>Price</span><span><span class="ef-swatch" style="background:var(--vd-s3)"></span>Electricity</span></div>
  <p class="vx-strip" id="ef-tco-summary"></p>
</section>

<div class="vx-grid vx-grid-2">
  <section class="vx-card">
    <h2>Efficiency by launch year</h2>
    <div id="ef-trend-chart" class="vd-chart" role="img" aria-label="Best and median points per rated watt by launch year"><div class="vd-state">Loading chart…</div></div>
    <div class="vx-legend vx-legend-left"><span><span class="ef-swatch" style="background:var(--vd-s3)"></span>Best</span><span><span class="ef-swatch" style="background:var(--vd-s1)"></span>Median</span></div>
  </section>
  <section class="vx-card">
    <h2>Rated power by launch year</h2>
    <div id="ef-watts-chart" class="vd-chart" role="img" aria-label="Median rated power by launch year"><div class="vd-state">Loading chart…</div></div>
    <p class="vx-muted">Is the label creeping up? Median rated power of the <span class="ef-kind">GPU</span>s launched each year that have a Blender score.</p>
  </section>
</div>

<section class="ef-measured" data-ef-for="cpu" aria-label="Measured server power">
  <div class="ef-measured-head">
    <span class="ef-badge">Measured</span>
    <h2>Server processors under a power meter</h2>
    <p class="vx-muted">SPECpower_ssj2008 reads the wall power of a whole server at every load from 100% down to idle. Results are grouped by the processor each disclosure names, and never ranked against the desktop chips above.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="vx-hero ef-sp-hero">
    <div class="vx-tile"><span class="vx-tile-label">Most efficient processor</span><span class="vx-tile-value ef-small" id="ef-sp-best"></span><span class="vx-tile-note" id="ef-sp-best-note"></span></div>
    <div class="vx-tile"><span class="vx-tile-label">Frontier doubles every</span><span class="vx-tile-value" id="ef-sp-double"></span><span class="vx-tile-note">Fit to the yearly best result, last six years</span></div>
    <div class="vx-tile"><span class="vx-tile-label">Idle draw</span><span class="vx-tile-value" id="ef-sp-idle"></span><span class="vx-tile-note" id="ef-sp-idle-note"></span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="vx-grid vx-grid-2">
    <section class="vx-card">
      <h2>Measured efficiency by year</h2>
      <div id="ef-sp-trend" class="vd-chart" role="img" aria-label="Best and median measured ssj_ops per watt by year of publication"><div class="vd-state">Loading chart…</div></div>
      <div class="vx-legend vx-legend-left"><span><span class="ef-swatch" style="background:var(--vd-s3)"></span>Best</span><span><span class="ef-swatch" style="background:var(--vd-s1)"></span>Median</span></div>
    </section>
    <section class="vx-card">
      <h2>Efficiency across the load range</h2>
      <div id="ef-sp-curve" class="vd-chart" role="img" aria-label="Measured ssj_ops per watt at each target load for the top processors"><div class="vd-state">Loading chart…</div></div>
      <p class="vx-muted">Servers spend most of their time well below full load. A flat curve keeps its efficiency when the work runs out.</p>
    </section>
  </div>
  <section class="vx-card">
    <div class="vx-card-head"><h2>Processors by measured efficiency</h2>
      <label class="vx-field ef-inline"><span class="visually-hidden">Maker</span><select id="ef-sp-vendor"><option value="all">All makers</option><option>AMD</option><option>Intel</option><option>Ampere</option></select></label></div>
    <div id="ef-sp-table" class="ef-table-wrap"></div>
    <p class="vx-fine">Median of each processor's SPECpower results. Idle share is active-idle power as a share of full-load power: lower means the server gets closer to drawing nothing when it has nothing to do.</p>
  </section>
</section>

<section class="ef-measured" data-ef-for="gpu" aria-label="Measured AI inference power">
  <div class="ef-measured-head">
    <span class="ef-badge">Measured</span>
    <h2>AI inference under a power meter</h2>
    <p class="vx-muted">MLPerf® Inference Power measures the whole system while it runs the benchmark. Few submitters measure power, so this panel is small. Each comparison uses the same benchmark and scenario.</p>
  </div>
  {MLPERF_HTML}
</section>
</div>
""")
```
